note: The dashboard decides what a parent is told about the machine. Its mutants are the wrong sentences, not generic operator swaps.

mutants.note: the master switch stops being consulted, so a daemon with enforcement off tells the parent the child is sitting at a locked screen when nothing will touch it
an open override stops suppressing the row, so the unlock the parent just granted shows as still-locked-out
the account's own switch stops being consulted. Distinct from B1: the fix is a checkbox on this row, not the daemon-wide kill switch
every row that reaches the default branch claims to be held, whatever the schedule says
a managed account whose profile is gone is rendered as an ordinary 'not locked out', which is the fail-open reading of a broken configuration
a profile read in the machine's zone because its own did not resolve keeps its verdict and loses the warning, so the parent believes a fallback is their setting
a schedule being silently unenforced stops counting as a gap in coverage
the count of held accounts includes accounts that are not being held, so the headline number disagrees with every row under it
an expired override keeps suppressing enforcement forever, which is a permanent unlock granted by a fifteen-minute one
every account without an override is shown as having had one that ran out, which is the same lie told in the other direction from B11
an override that ran out vanishes from the row, so a parent cannot tell 'nobody unlocked this child' from 'the unlock I made twenty minutes ago expired'
an inactive row carries the verdict's end time and rule name
mutants.equivalent: equivalent today, and kept as insurance: schedule.Evaluate assigns EndsAt and Rule only inside the branch that sets Active (schedule.go:175-180), so an inactive verdict's are already zero and nil and the guard changes no output. It stays because the row's contract should not depend on an upstream invariant that a future 'next end' field would silently break -- and if that field ever appears, this mutant stops being equivalent and starts being a real catch

mutants.note: the row names the rule's id instead of the name the parent typed, so the banner quotes a slug
every session lands on one bucket, so a child's row shows somebody else's locked screen

mutants.old: sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool { return rows[i].Username < rows[j].Username })
mutants.note: rows come back in config order, so the page reorders itself between two loads on a phone
the banner quotes a lockout time while the daemon is switched off, which is a time at which nothing happens
a held account produces the 'nobody is locked out' banner, the single most damaging sentence this page can print
the banner gives a time but not the rule, so the school-night rule and the weekend rule the parent forgot cannot be told apart
the banner says who is held and never says for how long
the banner names one held child and stays silent about the others, so a parent fixing the named one leaves the rest locked
a disabled account supplies the 'locked out again at' time, announcing a lockout that will never happen
the first row wins regardless of when it opens, so the banner quotes a later window than the one that is actually next
the clock is rendered in UTC rather than the profile's own zone, so a child on another zone is shown a minute that is not the minute their screen locks
with nothing scheduled and a profile that could not be read, the banner says no window is scheduled -- the fail-open reading of a broken profile
